content.overview: Article 243E provides that every Panchayat, unless sooner dissolved under any law, shall continue for five years from the date appointed for its first meeting. No amendment of a law in force shall have the effect of causing dissolution of a Panchayat at any level until the expiration of its duration. An election to constitute a Panchayat shall be completed before the expiry of its duration or before the expiration of six months from dissolution; if the remainder of the period would be less than six months after dissolution, it is not necessary to hold election for that period. A Panchayat constituted upon dissolution continues only for the remainder of the period.
content.glance: Panchayat term: 5 years from first meeting. Election before expiry or within 6 months of dissolution. Short remainder (<6 months) after dissolution: election not mandatory for that remainder.
content.study:
Article 243E duration and elections:
1. Duration: **five years** from the date appointed for the first meeting (unless sooner dissolved).
2. Law amendment cannot dissolve a sitting Panchayat before end of its duration.
3. Election to constitute a Panchayat: completed **before** expiry of duration, or before expiry of **six months** from dissolution.
4. If post-dissolution remainder of term is **less than six months**, election for that remainder is not necessary.
5. Panchayat elected after dissolution sits only for the remainder of the original period.

Examination: 5-year term; election timing; 6-month rule; remainder period.

sections.heading: Duration and elections
sections.body:
1. Five-year term from first meeting (unless sooner dissolved).
2. Election before expiry of term or within 6 months of dissolution.
3. Remainder <6 months after dissolution: election for remainder not required.
4. Post-dissolution Panchayat sits only for remainder of original period.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What is the duration of a Panchayat under Article 243E?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 243E, every Panchayat, unless sooner dissolved under any law for the time being in force, shall continue for five years from the date appointed for its first meeting. An election to constitute a Panchayat shall be completed before the expiry of its duration or before the expiration of a period of six months from the date of its dissolution. Where the remainder of the period for which the dissolved Panchayat would have continued is less than six months, it is not necessary to hold any election for constituting the Panchayat for such period. A Panchayat constituted upon dissolution continues only for the remainder of the period for which the dissolved Panchayat would have continued.

examTips: 5-year term; election before expiry or within 6 months of dissolution.

keyTakeaways: Art 243E: five-year duration of Panchayats and election timing.
